newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale promoted to Natural Resources portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Goodale promoted to Natural Resources portfolio.

text.p: Ralph Goodale, formerly Agriculture Minister and one of the few western Canadian Liberals in the cabinet, on Wednesday was handed responsibility for the high-profile Natural Resources Ministry.
Goodale, from Saskatchewan, takes over from fellow westerner Anne McLellan, an Albertan who was widely respected by her province's energy industry.
The oil and gas industry will be watching to see if Goodale, who is well-respected within the ruling Liberal Party caucus makes any changes to the government's greenhouse gas policy.

The energy industry -- Canada's third largest emitter of greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane -- undertook voluntary measures two years ago to cut emissions. The industry argues it must be given enough time to improve its performance without invoking government-mandated caps.
Voluntary reductions were a main plank in former minister Anne McLellan's energy policy.
Goodale will also retain responsibility for the Canadian Wheat Board, one of the world's oldest and largest state commodity export monopolies.

As agriculture minister under the last parliament, Goodale said if he were reappointed to the position, he would reintroduce amendments to the CWB Act, which propose to modernize the CWB's governance to a farmer-elected board of directors from the current government-appointed commissioners.

Under Goodale's plan, membership in the CWB would still be mandatory. The new government will likely face competing pressures from the farming sector, with one side backing a continued mandatory monopoly and the other side pushing for a voluntary organization.
Canada is the second largest seller of wheat to the world. The CWB, Canada's fifth largest exporter, made C$5.8 billion in wheat and barley sales in the 1995/96 crop year (Aug/July).
Goodale, from Saskatchewan, becomes natural resources minister at a time when Cameco Corp plans to develop the huge McArthur River uranium mine in that province.
The deposit is the largest high-grade uranium orebody known in the world, Cameco says.
The province of Saskatchewan has already approved the project, but federal approval has yet to come.
